Independent continuant/minor derivation, log-concavity and uniform perturbation argument
correctness.rationale: The rank-one approximation is positive and trace class even though K itself is not (K≥I/(μ+4)); differentiation of the bounded resolvent gives capture −∂μ log K_jj. Independently recovered the half-line diagonal by reflecting the infinite-line resolvent across −1/2, and the finite one by principal minors: the determinant of the first k<n rows/columns is (q^(−k)+q^(k+1))/(1+q) by the continuant recurrence; applying the second degree-one endpoint row gives the full determinant (1−q)(q^(−n)−q^n)/(1+q). Cramer's rule gives the stated product of the two boundary factors; log differentiation proves both capture formulas. The odd-index sequence f_a is strictly log-concave and tends to zero, so a neighboring equality at a simple root of a−(a+2)q²−2q^(a+2) is an exact two-site maximum; at that root the next neighboring difference is strictly positive, which orders the thresholds. The continuous maximum of a↦f_a is at aβ=c; Rolle gives c/(a+2)<β_j<c/a and each discrete maximum is within two in a of the continuous one for small β. With μ=β²+O(β⁴) this gives both stated scaling results. On the left half of each finite path, the right-image term goes to zero uniformly on compact positive-β intervals. A strict half-line gap persists uniformly near each fixed threshold: truncate the uniformly vanishing half-line tail and use continuity on the finitely many remaining sites. Thus only the adjacent reflected pairs compete. Their contrast is D_a+f_b−f_(b−2), b=2n−a. Its derivative converges uniformly to D'_a on such a neighborhood, giving a unique crossing, and the mean-value theorem gives its displacement as −(f_b−f_(b−2))(β_j)/(d_j+o(1)). Since the numerator contrast is −(e^(2β_j)−1)b e^(−bβ_j)(1+o(1)), the displacement is upwards with the stated coefficient after changing to μ. At β_0=log 2 the derivative is 2/3 and ∂βμ=3/2, yielding 27/4. The same uniform gap gives stability away from thresholds.
residual_risks: The packaged checker only brackets the normalized finite shift between 0 and 2 on sampled sizes, not asymptotic equivalence; the latter follows from the analytic mean-value argument. High-precision order and Rolle checks use 50 odd parameters, with an additional parameter in the sign-bracket test. No finite all-n phase diagram or limit uniform in increasing j is established or claimed.

evidence: On a finite path the rank-one score is both captured trace and reduction of the total diagonal of the conditional covariance (Schur complement) after observing one site in the screened Gaussian covariance. Fornace–Lindsey eqs. (3)–(4) and §2.2 give this general equivalence.

Maximizing the Green diagonal (one-site determinant) is not maximizing −∂μ log of that diagonal. On the half-line the diagonal itself is strictly largest at the endpoint for every μ, whereas the trace optimum can be arbitrarily deep.

value.rationale: The exact optimum and its dependence on screening answer a natural one-landmark problem for a canonical graph, and the winner is not the one chosen by the simpler determinant criterion. The infinite staircase with tie rules, the diverging optimum depth constant, and the signed sharp shift show both boundary behavior and when a long finite path reproduces it. This is useful exact information beyond solving the tridiagonal recurrence or showing that the endpoint is sometimes optimal.
residual_risks: No multi-column, nonuniform-conductance, or fixed-n global phase assertion is warranted.
